examples.label: Exploit CVE-2014-3704 to create a new admin account

notes: Drupal 7 < 7.32 SQLi (CVE-2014-3704). It creates an admin account rather than direct RCE, so follow up by logging in and planting a webshell.
name: Drupalgeddon - Create Admin (CVE-2014-3704)
description: Exploits the Drupalgeddon SQL injection (Drupal 7 < 7.32) to create a new administrator account, giving full CMS control.

defense.why_it_works: Drupalgeddon (SA-CORE-2014-005 / CVE-2014-3704) exploits SQL injection in Drupal's database abstraction layer. Array-format username parameters bypass query sanitization, allowing insertion of a new admin user without authentication.
defense.prerequisites: Drupal 7.x before 7.32. Unauthenticated access to the registration or login endpoint.
defense.impact: Creates a new admin-level user, providing full backend access for further exploitation (webshell, data exfiltration).
defense.detection: Unusual POST parameters with array notation to Drupal's login endpoint. New admin user in the database. drupalgeddon.py request pattern.
defense.artifacts: Web server access logs (POST with array parameters) | Database: new user in users table with admin role | Drupal watchdog log (new user registration)
defense.prevention: Update to Drupal 7.32+. This vulnerability is over 10 years old -- any unpatched Drupal 7 instance should be considered fully compromised.
defense.misconfiguration: Drupal 7.x < 7.32 running on a public-facing server without the SA-CORE-2014-005 patch applied.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Drupal 7.x < 7.32
# Vulnerable query in includes/database/database.inc
# No parameterised query for array-type form values
defense.secure_config:
# Update to Drupal 7.32+ or Drupal 9.x
drush pm-update drupal
defense.evasion: Rename/obfuscate the uploaded webshell and delete it after use; prefer the app's built-in functionality (PHP filter / module) over dropping files; pace requests to blend with normal traffic.
